newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec housing starts off but year best since 88.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec housing starts off but year best since 88.

text.p: Construction starts on new homes and apartments slowed sharply during December to the slowest rate in 1-1/2 years, the Commerce Department said Wednesday, ending a strong building year on a weak note.
Total starts plunged 12.2 percent last month to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.329 million, the weakest building rate since 1.301 million in June 1995.
Despite the drop in December starts, which likely were affected by severe winter weather in parts of the country, construction for the full year 1996 was exceptionally strong.
The total 1.474 million homes started in 1996 was the briskest building rate in eight years, since construction was started on 1.488 million new homes in 1988.
The falloff in starts during December was more abrupt than anticipated by Wall Street economists who had forecast starts at a rate of 1.47 million a year.
Every region reported a lower rate of starts last month, though the biggest drop occurred in the West where starts plummeted 29.2 percent to an annual rate of 257,000.
It was the lowest annual starts rate for new homes in the West, which includes the big California market, since February 1993 when the rate also was 257,000, Commerce officials said.
Bitter weather including heavy snow and flooding affected parts of the West in December and continued into January.

Starts in the Northeast were down 2.3 percent in December to a rate of 125,000 a year and in the Midwest they fell 7.9 percent to 302,000. Construction starts in the South, the biggest regional market, dropped 7.2 percent last month to an annual rate of 645,000.
The weaker pace of building is expected to continue into the early months of 1997, though no precipitous decline is foreseen.
New permit applications eased in December by 0.6 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.41 million but that followed a 4.1 percent increase in November.
The National Association of Home Builders said last week that its index of market activity was down moderately in January but added that the market appeared to be steadying.

"The housing market has been basically stable for the past three months after a steady decline in the later part of 1996 from a much stronger level of demand earlier in the year," said assocation president Randy Smith, a builder in Walnut Creek, Calif.

Lower building rates in December occurred despite slightly cheaper mortgages in December. The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., or Freddie Mac, said rates for a 30-year loan averaged 7.6 percent in December, down from 7.62 percent in November.
